title: Long Vowel Teams
source: Science of Reading Level 7 Teacher Guide

units.title: ai
units.summary: Lesson 1A: ai spells long a at the beginning or in the middle of a word (rain, wait, paint). A vowel team is two or more letters that together represent a vowel sound. The ai and ay lessons are followed by a lesson with both together.

lessons.title: Phonemic awareness
lessons.notes: Hear the long a sound and isolate it in spoken words.

lessons.title: Teaching skill and model
lessons.notes: Build words with the vowel team tile; two or more letters make one vowel sound.

lessons.title: Encoding and decoding
lessons.notes: Sound boxes and mapping; read and spell words from the list.

lessons.title: Guided practice
lessons.notes: Word lists, sentences, dictation.

lessons.title: High-frequency words
lessons.notes: wait; irregular: said

lessons.title: More practice
lessons.notes: Open and closed word sorts, student workbook pages.

objectives.text: read words like rain, wait, paint and snail with the ai vowel team
say that ai spells long a in the middle of a word
spell words such as mail, train and tail using ai
read the common words wait and said

replaces: Vowel Teams · Long a: ai, ay

units.title: ay
units.summary: Lessons 1B and 1C: ay spells long a at the end of a word (day, play, stay). Then ai and ay are practised together, choosing by position. High-frequency words: day, way, play, say, wait; irregular: says, said.

lessons.title: Phonemic awareness
lessons.notes: Hear the long a sound and isolate it in spoken words.

lessons.title: Teaching skill and model
lessons.notes: Build words with the vowel team tile; two or more letters make one vowel sound.

lessons.title: Encoding and decoding
lessons.notes: Sound boxes and mapping; read and spell words from the list.

lessons.title: Guided practice
lessons.notes: Word lists, sentences, dictation.

lessons.title: High-frequency words
lessons.notes: day, way, play, say, wait; irregular: says, said

lessons.title: More practice
lessons.notes: Open and closed word sorts, student workbook pages.

lessons.title: Lesson 1C: ai and ay together
lessons.notes: Sort words by position and spell with the right team.

objectives.text: read words like day, play, stay and tray with the ay vowel team
choose ai or ay by where the sound comes in the word
spell words like pay, clay and spray using ay
read the common words day, way, play and say

units.title: ee
units.summary: Lesson 2A: ee spells long e, usually in the middle but also at the end (see, tree, feet). Students will learn later that y also spells /ē/ at the end of longer words (happy), which links to the suffix -y. High-frequency words: green, sleep, three, need, keep, feet, week, feel.

lessons.title: Phonemic awareness
lessons.notes: Hear the long e sound and isolate it in spoken words.

lessons.title: Teaching skill and model
lessons.notes: Build words with the vowel team tile; two or more letters make one vowel sound.

lessons.title: Encoding and decoding
lessons.notes: Sound boxes and mapping; read and spell words from the list.

lessons.title: Guided practice
lessons.notes: Word lists, sentences, dictation.

lessons.title: High-frequency words
lessons.notes: green, sleep, three, need, keep, feet, week, feel

lessons.title: More practice
lessons.notes: Open and closed word sorts, student workbook pages.

objectives.text: read words like see, tree, feet and sleep with the ee vowel team
spell words such as green, keep, week and queen using ee
hear that y can also say long e at the end of a longer word, like happy
read the common words green, three, need, keep and feel

replaces: Vowel Teams · Long e: ee, ea

units.title: ea
units.summary: Lessons 2B and 2C: ea also spells long e (eat, seat, beach). There is no trick to decide between ee and ea when spelling; over time students remember them, and the homophone lesson helps. ee and ea are practised together. High-frequency words: real, read, eat, each, means, please, leave, near, year.

lessons.title: Lesson 2C: ee and ea together

objectives.text: read words like eat, seat, beach and teach with the ea vowel team

read the common words real, eat, each, please and year

units.title: oa
units.summary: Lesson 3A: oa spells long o at the beginning or in the middle of a word (boat, soap, road). Word family -oad is practised with the ow and oe lessons.

units.title: ow and oe
units.summary: Lessons 3B and 3C: ow spells long o at the end of a word (snow, show, grow) except in a few words like shown, grown and own; oe at the end of a few words (toe, hoe, goes). oa, ow and oe are then practised together. High-frequency words: grow, show, know, own (goes, though).

lessons.title: Lesson 3C: oa, ow and oe together

objectives.text: read words like snow, grow, slow and toe with the ow and oe vowel teams
choose oa, ow or oe by where the sound comes in the word
spell words such as blow, window and toe
read the common words grow, show, know and own

units.title: igh and ie
units.summary: Lesson 4: igh spells long i, usually in the middle of a word followed by t (night, light) and at the end of a few words (high, thigh, sigh). The g and h are silent. ie spells long i at the end of a few words (pie, tie, lie, die). High-frequency words: high, might, light, night, right; irregular: eye, buy.

units.title: Review of long vowel teams
units.summary: Review Lessons 1 to 4: ai, ay, ee, ea, oa, ow, oe, igh and ie read and spelled together, with word sorts, a review of the dropping y rule, and spelling and reading assessments.

lessons.title: Mixed review
lessons.notes: Read and spell words with all of the long vowel teams taught so far.

lessons.title: Spelling
lessons.notes: Choosing among teams for the same sound.

lessons.title: Review pages
lessons.notes: Workbook review and word sorts.

objectives.text: read words that mix ai, ay, ee, ea, oa, ow and igh without stopping to decode
choose among the spellings of a long vowel sound in dictated words
spell two-syllable words that contain a long vowel team, such as rainbow and teacher
add the prefixes re- and un- to words, like redo and unlock

units.title: Other sounds of ea
units.summary: Lessons 5A and 5B. ea does not always say long e: it can say short e (bread, head, deaf, meant) and, in a few words, long a (steak, break, great; optional). Teach the few long a words as heart words for now.

lessons.title: Lesson 5A: ea says short e
lessons.notes: Read and sort words like head, bread and deaf.

lessons.title: Lesson 5B: ea says long a (optional)
lessons.notes: Not a full lesson; add on to the last lesson or teach as heart words.

lessons.title: Practice
lessons.notes: Read ea words and decide which sound it makes.

objectives.text: know that ea can say short e as well as long e, as in head and eat
read words like bread, head, deaf and meant
read the long a ea words steak, break and great
sort ea words by the sound the letters make

units.title: ie says long e
units.summary: Lesson 6. ie can also spell long e in the middle of a word (field, chief, thief, piece), which is different from ie at the end of a word (pie), where it says long i.

lessons.title: Teaching skill
lessons.notes: ie says long e in the middle of a word (field) and long i at the end (pie).

lessons.title: Read and spell
lessons.notes: Words with ie in the middle; word sorts.

lessons.title: Review
lessons.notes: ie and other long e teams.

objectives.text: read words like field, chief, thief and shield with ie saying long e
tell ie at the end of pie from ie in the middle of field
spell words such as brief, niece and piece
sort long e words by their spelling: ee, ea or ie

replaces: Vowel Teams · Long e: ie; other sounds of ea

units.title: Homophones
units.summary: Lesson 7. Homophones sound the same but are spelled differently and mean different things (see and sea, meet and meat, no and know, write and right). Because ee and ea cannot be told apart by sound, learning the meaning is how students choose the spelling. High-frequency words: know, knew, write, wrote.

lessons.title: Homophones
lessons.notes: Pairs of words with the same sound and different spelling and meaning; use each in a sentence.

lessons.title: Sorting
lessons.notes: Sort pairs by meaning and by spelling pattern.

lessons.title: Silent letters
lessons.notes: The silent letters in words such as know, write and sign.

lessons.title: Practice
lessons.notes: Spell the right word for the sentence.

objectives.text: tell homophones like sea and see, meet and meat apart by meaning
choose the correct spelling of a homophone for a sentence
read and spell words with silent letters like knee, write and gnat
use apostrophes to read and write contractions like can't and it's

replaces: Multisyllable & Morphology · Digraphs & ghost sounds: ph, gn, mb

units.title: ei says long a
units.summary: Optional extra lesson 8. ei says long a in a few words, often with silent gh (eight, weigh, neighbor, veil). The eigh pattern is taught with its silent letters.

lessons.title: Teaching skill
lessons.notes: ei says long a; show the eigh tile with its silent gh.

lessons.title: Read and spell
lessons.notes: eight, weigh, veil, vein and similar words.

objectives.text: read words like eight, weigh, veil and vein where ei says long a
notice the silent gh in eight and weigh
spell the numbers eight and eighty

units.title: Suffixes -ful and -less
units.summary: Lessons on -ful and -less: both make adjectives (hopeful, helpless). Words with a suffix: circle the base word and the suffix. Other adjective suffixes -y, -able and -ible are practised with these.

lessons.title: Introduce
lessons.notes: -ful (full of) and -less (without) added to base words.

lessons.title: Reading and spelling
lessons.notes: Words like careful, helpless, painful, joyful.

lessons.title: Reading sentences
lessons.notes: Circle the base word and suffix.

objectives.text: say that -ful means full of and -less means without
read words like careful, helpful, hopeless and painless
add -ful or -less to a base word and use it in a sentence
sort words with -ful, -less, -y, -able and -ible by suffix

units.title: Suffixes -ly and -ness
units.summary: Lessons on -ly and -ness: -ly usually makes adverbs (how) and -ness makes nouns (quality of). Words with more than one suffix, like deeply and playfully, are broken into base and suffixes.

lessons.title: Introduce
lessons.notes: -ly (how) and -ness (quality of) added to base words.

lessons.title: Reading and spelling
lessons.notes: Words like slowly, kindness, sadly, darkness.

lessons.title: Double suffixes
lessons.notes: Circle each suffix in deeply and playfully.

objectives.text: say that -ly tells how and -ness names a quality, as in slowly and kindness
read words like quickly, sadness, loudly and darkness
add -ly or -ness to a base word and use it in a sentence
break a word with two suffixes, like playfully, into its parts

replaces: Multisyllable & Morphology · Suffix -al/-ial (final stable cial, tial)
